notes: Pinned inputs of the release build (packaging/build-release.mjs). Every download is official, unmodified and checked against the SHA-256 recorded here. See docs/PACKAGING.md.

runtimeBase.notes: previousRelease: the release before the one being built (the release script sets it with every version). It names the Update zip: when `required` equals it the update covers one release and is AI-NPC-LLM-Companions-Update-<required>-to-<version>.zip, when `required` is older it covers several and is AI-NPC-LLM-Companions-Update-<required>-and-up-to-<version>.zip (packaging/lib/full-package.mjs updateFrom; a Scripts build stops when previousRelease is missing or does not fit). required: The oldest Runtime base these Scripts run on (written as runtimeBase into the Scripts' release.json and code.json). From 0.3.4 the Scripts carry all of the mod's code (docs/PACKAGING.md, 'Code in the Scripts') and the Runtime is the base: Node, Python, llama.cpp, vgmstream, Playwright, the models, the voices, the game archives. Raise it to the new version only in a release that changes the base (a new Runtime update zip in updates/ then carries the change); the setup check and the version notice name it to a player whose Runtime is older. 0.3.3: a Runtime of 0.3.3 holds everything the 0.3.4 code needs (its own old code is replaced at the first start).

limits.notes: assetBytes: a Scripts or Runtime zip is closed and continued in another before it passes this (the GitHub release's 2 GiB limit). githubFileBytes: a single file that large in those packages stops the build. The optional packs (OmniVoice, Local AI, Mature) are hosted on Hugging Face as ONE zip each and have no limit here: no parts, no split files.

packFiles.notes: The file names of the optional packs (owner decision 2026-10-28: every model pack carries the model's name and parameter count in its file name). Pattern: <Type>-<Tier>-<Model>-<Params> (OmniPack-<Model>-<Params> and PocketTTS-Model-<Params>-<Language> have no tier). `title` is the name a build writes (<title>-<version>.zip) and the name on Hugging Face (<folder>/<title>.zip, no version). `legacyTitle` is the name before 0.3.4: detection never depended on a zip's name (the packs are found by the markers and folders inside them, so a pack installed from an old name works unchanged), but the uploader still accepts a build folder that holds the old name, and the old Hugging Face paths stay valid for a transition. packaging/lib/pack-names.mjs and packaging/upload-packs.py read this block; a test keeps it equal to the model names pinned below. The three vision files (owner decision 2026-10-29: a vision projector is a SEPARATE small download, not part of a pack) have no tier and no legacy title: <Type>-<Model>-<Params>-projector, in the vision/ subfolder of the folder of the packs that need them (alsoIn: the same zip is published at a second path, the Gemma 4 E4B projector serves Local AI standard and Mature standard). See visionFiles below. docs/PACKAGING.md, 'Pack file names'.

omniModel.notes: `files` are the upstream files at the pinned revision, each checked against its size and SHA-256. The pack ships every one of them unmodified except model.safetensors: that file is rounded from float32 to float16 by packaging/convert-omni-fp16.py (the precision the voice engine loads it in: the VoiceStudio adapter's model_manager passes dtype=torch.float16 and bridge/resident-voice-worker.py refuses any other), 1,225,189,208 bytes instead of 2,450,344,112. `converted` pins the result; the conversion is deterministic, so the build checks the converted file against it. The audio tokenizer is NOT converted: OmniVoice loads it without a dtype (it runs as float32; its config.json says float32) and a float16 file would change the audio.

vgmstream.notes: vgmstream-cli decodes the Wwise voice-over of a player's V voice mod (bridge/ reads it one line at a time, on the player's PC, and the process exits after the build). Shipped in the Runtime at app/<runtimeFolder>/: the unmodified files of the official vgmstream Windows release (the release also has swresample and zlib-ng DLLs, which the voice-over decode does not need, and plugins for media players: none of those are shipped). The build reads them from <repo>/vendor/vgmstream/ (git-ignored; no download) and checks each against the size and SHA-256 recorded here. The licence texts are committed in packaging/licenses/vgmstream/ and go to app/<licenceFolder>/ (a licence text is hashed with its line ends as LF, so a checkout with CRLF or LF checks the same).

native.notes: The optional native plugin (native/core, docs/NATIVE_REWRITE_PLAN.md). The package works without the DLL: the Lua keeps its own path. runtime/native-off.txt is the kill switch and always ships; `off` lists the systems that start off because they are not yet proven in the real game (one name per line in the file, a missing file means all on). The list is empty: every native system is on.

localAi.notes: The two optional Local AI downloads (docs/LOCAL_AI.md, docs/LOCAL_MODEL_CHOICE.md), hosted on Hugging Face, in its local-ai/ folder, as one zip each. The llama.cpp engine (server, llama-fit-params, libraries) ships in the RUNTIME, in app/<server.runtimeFolder>/ (server.inPacks is false since 0.2.9: the packs carry models only and their manifests name no server, so they need the Runtime of 0.2.7 or newer; set it true and each pack carries a copy in llama/ again, for a pack used with an older Runtime). Each pack carries the embedding model and its own chat model whole (no parts), plus a manifest fragment that bridge/local-ai-pack.mjs merges. Every file is the unmodified upstream file, checked against the SHA-256 recorded here. Each chat model has a vision projector (`mmproj` on the tier: the Q8_0 projector made for that model, pinned the same way). It is NOT in the pack: it is a separate small zip (visionFiles below, the vision/ folder of local-ai on Hugging Face), written to models/ beside the model when the player extracts it. The pack's manifest only NAMES it (`mmproj: 'models/<file>'`), so bridge/local-llm-server.mjs loads it without guessing when it is there, and tells the player where to get it when it is not (only while Companions can see is on, docs/LOCAL_AI.md, 'Pictures'). packaging/lib/pack-projector.mjs checks its size and hash when the zip is built. With --models local, a developer folder (--local-ai-source, or CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_LOCAL_AI_DEV) is used instead of downloading, and each file in it is checked against the same hash.

voiceClips.notes: fromGame false: the Runtime and the OmniVoice pack carry the voice reference clips as before. true: they carry none, and the player's PC builds each character's clips from the game's own English voice files when the character is first invited or talked to (bridge/voice-clips.mjs, characters/voice-clips-manifest.json, docs/VOICE_EXTRACTION.md), or downloads them from the Hugging Face repository (voice-clips/<kind>/<key>.wav, the list is packaging/voice-clips-upload-list.json). Do not turn it on before that list is uploaded.

omniPack.notes: The OmniVoice pack (docs/PACKAGING.md, 'The OmniVoice pack'). `runtimeClips`: the reference clips the RUNTIME carries for the 60 voices added after the pack was frozen (path, size, CRC-32 of each). The Mistral voice (Voxtral) reads them for players without this pack, so they stay in the Runtime; the pack leaves them out, so the Runtime and the pack never ship the same file (packaging/check-pack-overlap.mjs). A build from scratch skips those paths and stops when the clip it would skip differs from the listed bytes.

visionFiles.notes: The vision projectors of the Local AI and Mature models as SEPARATE downloads (owner decision 2026-10-29, replacing the first version that put each projector inside its pack). One small zip per projector, named <Type>-<Model>-<Params>-projector (packFiles above), holding the file at <layout.localAiDirectory>/models/<file> (where the bridge looks, beside the model), the Apache-2.0 text, a notice and a receipt (vision-<id>.json, which also lets the pack placer find a zip that was extracted one folder too deep). The file is the projector pinned as `mmproj` on the tier named by `pin` (a dotted path in this file), so the pin, the size check and the hash check are the same as ever (packaging/lib/pack-projector.mjs). `usedBy` lists the packs whose manifests name the file; `owner` is who made the model for the notice. The packs themselves hold no projector: their manifests name it (`mmproj`), and the main mod tells the player once, only while Companions can see is on, where to get a missing one (the vision/ folder of local-ai or mature on the Hugging Face packs page). Built with --packages vision-gemma,vision-bonsai,vision-qwen (never in the default set, never on Nexus Mods as a file of its own).

maturePack.notes: The optional Mature packs (docs/LOCAL_AI.md, 'Mature content'; packaging/MATURE_PACK_README.md): two optional downloads, Mature lite and Mature standard, each ONE zip holding one uncensored model file (lite and good like the Local AI packs) and its own marker (manifest.mature-lite.json, manifest.mature-standard.json) that the main mod reads to say in the setting's help whether a Mature model is installed and to offer it in the Local AI model row (turning Mature content on selects the good one if it fits, else the lite one); each works alone, and the Mature content setting itself is part of the main mod and works without the packs. They are distributed ONLY as files on the project's Hugging Face repository (alystria-ai/ai-npc-cyberpunk-mod-packs, in its mature/ folder; packaging/upload-packs.py), never on Nexus Mods and not on the GitHub release (packaging/MATURE_PACK_RELEASE_NOTES.md has the text for the Hugging Face page). The release workflow builds and uploads them only when its opt-in 'mature' input is set (never on a tag push), one matrix job per pack; by hand they are built with --packages mature-lite or mature-standard. They are never part of the default set, and nothing of them is in the Runtime package. Each Mature model has a vision projector too, as a separate small zip in the vision/ folder of mature on Hugging Face (visionFiles below, not part of the pack): the Gemma 4 E4B one for Mature standard is the same pinned file as the Local AI standard one (same path, same bytes, so extracting it twice overwrites identical bytes), and it loaded and described a picture with the fine-tune (docs/COMPANION_VISION.md, section 2c). The Qwen3.5-4B one for Mature lite is the 644 MiB BF16 file of the model's own repository, pinned at the model's revision, downloaded 2026-10-29 and checked to load and describe a picture with the installed Mature lite model (docs/COMPANION_VISION.md, section 2d). Both models are pinned by revision, size and SHA-256 from the Hugging Face file listing (2026-10-14; both downloaded, SHA-256 checked and run in docs/MATURE_SAMPLES_V3_2026-10-14.md); 'remote' is the file's path inside the repository when it is in a folder. They were chosen from the community data in docs/MATURE_MODELS_V2_2026-10-14.md and confirmed with scripts/Eval-MatureSamples.mjs (third round: docs/MATURE_SAMPLES_V3_2026-10-14.md).

mirror.notes: Copies of the two model files in the private bucket (outside final/, so the trained-model fetch never downloads them), so a takedown of the community repositories cannot break a build. --models hf takes each model from here (SHA-256 checked against the pins above) and falls back to the pinned public URL when the mirror lacks it.

micPacks.notes: The two optional voice-input packs (docs/LOCAL_STT.md, 'The optional packs'; docs/PACKAGING.md, 'Voice-input packs'): MicPack-European (NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3, int8) and MicPack-Asian (SenseVoice Small, int8: Mandarin Chinese, Japanese, Korean). Each is ONE zip hosted on Hugging Face in its mic/ folder, never on Nexus Mods and not on the GitHub release; the workflow builds them only when its opt-in 'micpacks' input is set (never on a tag push), and by hand they are built with --packages micpack-european,micpack-asian. They are never part of the default set and nothing of them is in the Runtime package. A pack puts its model files in app/models/stt/<id>/ (bridge/local-stt.mjs resolveLocalSttPaths looks there), beside the Runtime's own app/models/stt/moonshine-tiny-en-int8/, which they never touch. Every model file is the unmodified file of the sherpa-onnx 'asr-models' release archive named below: the build downloads that archive from its pinned URL (SHA-256 checked), extracts only the files listed here from it (the archive is untrusted data: nothing in it is run, and a path outside the extraction folder stops the build) and checks each extracted file against the size and SHA-256 recorded here. test_wavs and the archive's README are never shipped. With --mic-pack-source DIR (or CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_MIC_PACKS_DEV) a developer folder laid out as DIR/<pack id>/<file> is used instead of the download, and each file in it is checked against the same pins. Sizes and hashes measured 2026-10-19 from the real files. The licence of each model is kept in the pack's NOTICE.txt; a licence that is only linked (the FunASR Model Open Source License) is linked there and is not copied into the pack.

devOnlyLuaNotes: Added with Music and TV: media-probe.lua is a feature of johnny-probe.lua (scripts/Send-JohnnyProbe.ps1 media read), loaded only the same way, with Developer mode on; the shipped media-context.lua does not load it. Added in 0.2.9: johnny-probe.lua (with its two feature files johnny-relic-probe.lua and combat-feats-probe.lua) is loaded only by init.lua's guarded pcall(dofile, ...) with Developer mode on and a johnny-probe request that scripts/Send-JohnnyProbe.ps1 writes; fact-identity.lua is loaded only by diagnostics.lua; knowledge-state.lua is loaded by no Lua file (it is the Lua side of the retired native knowledge state: KnowledgeState.reds is in retiredRedscript and the bridge's knowledge-service.mjs is not in the Runtime). The Scripts zip is extracted over an old install, so a copy an earlier Scripts zip left stays in the player's folder, unused.
